summary: SIEM audit export: customer asks for audit category taxonomy + filter examples (allowlist/denylist, actor/resource predicates)
description:
Issue summary:
Quantiva Security Ops team is evaluating the SIEM-ready audit export beta (Splunk/S3) and asked for (a) the definitive category taxonomy for Audit Event Schema v2, and (b) concrete filter examples they can use to limit exported events to what their SOC needs (and minimize PII).

Customer questions (verbatim-ish from call + follow-up email):
1) “What are the exact category values, and are they stable?”
2) “Can we filter to only admin/console actions and exclude model inference traffic?”
3) “Can we do an allowlist for a few actions (e.g., workspace.user.invite, api_key.create) and denylist everything else?”
4) “Can we filter out fields like source_ip / user_agent, or at least exclude events where those are present?”
5) “Do you support filtering by actor email / resource name / prefix match?”

Impact:
Blocking customer from finalizing filter configuration for beta rollout. They need written guidance for internal change control.

Environment:
Prod (EU). Beta flag not yet enabled for tenant.

Request:
Provide category taxonomy + recommended “starter filters” with explanation of tradeoffs (compliance vs volume vs PII). If docs are missing/unclear, publish an authoritative list and examples we can share during beta.
comments: 2025-05-07 (Liam O'Rourke, Support): Created ticket from Quantiva thread. Assigning to Colin for SE-style guidance; looping Security/PM for canonical taxonomy + doc link we can share externally.

2025-05-07 (Colin O'Donnell, Solutions Engineer): Acknowledged. I can provide practical examples, but we need Marcus/Kevin to confirm the canonical category list + stability guarantees. Also need to be careful: we don’t currently support filtering that inspects presence of specific fields (e.g., “exclude events with source_ip present”).

2025-05-08 (Kevin Osei, Security Eng): Category values are intended to be stable (additive changes only during beta, no renames). Source of truth is Audit Event Schema v2 + taxonomy mapping. High-level buckets we’ve been using: auth, access, admin, data, model, billing, security, system. Some actions are also grouped under these.
PII: source_ip and user_agent are only populated for certain event types; we do not support filtering by presence of those fields today. If they need strict minimization, recommended approach is to filter out entire categories/actions that tend to include network context.
Also confirm: filtering is evaluated on event metadata (category/action + selected actor/resource fields), not on free-form payloads; this is intentional for safety and performance.

2025-05-08 (Naomi Feldman, PM): +1. We should publish a customer-shareable “Category taxonomy + example filters” section as part of beta docs/FAQ. Important clarifications:
- Filters are about what is exported, not what is retained in Redwood.
- During beta, categories/actions may expand but we’ll avoid breaking changes.
- Non-scope: regex / prefix match on arbitrary strings; no filtering on request bodies/prompt content.
I’ll track doc update separately; for now, Support can send a short list + examples with beta disclaimers.

2025-05-09 (Colin O'Donnell, Solutions Engineer): Draft response to customer (for Support to send):

1) Category taxonomy (Audit Schema v2)
We group audit events into stable categories used for filtering + SIEM mapping:
- auth: login/logout, SSO/SAML events, token/session lifecycle
- access: permission checks, membership changes (may overlap with admin depending on action)
- admin: workspace/org administration (settings, invites, role changes)
- security: key/secret lifecycle, export config changes, policy changes
- model: model access/config changes, routing policy changes (NOT per-request inference content)
- data: dataset/connectors (if applicable), artifacts metadata operations
- billing: plan/entitlement changes
- system: internal service operations relevant for compliance (rarely used in customer filters)

2) Filtering capabilities (beta)
Supported predicates:
- allowlist/denylist on category
- allowlist/denylist on action (exact match)
- resource.type + resource.id (exact match)
- actor.type (user/service) + actor.id (exact match)
- time window controls for backfill/replay

Not supported (beta):
- regex / prefix / contains matching on actor email, resource name, user_agent
- filtering on presence/absence of optional fields (e.g., source_ip)
- filtering on request payloads / prompts / generated text (prohibited)

3) Example “starter filters”
A) Admin-only (recommended first pass)
- allow categories: [admin, security, access]
- deny categories: [model, data, billing, system] (optional)

B) Narrow actions allowlist (high signal)
- allow actions: [workspace.user.invite, workspace.user.remove, workspace.role.update, api_key.create, api_key.revoke, audit_export.create, audit_export.update]
- deny categories: [system]

C) Exclude SSO chatter
- allow categories: [admin, security]
- deny categories: [auth]

Notes:
- Delivery is at-least-once; downstream should deduplicate by event_id.
- Category expansion may occur; if you need strict control, prefer an allowlist.

I’ll ask Docs to add these examples to the Splunk/S3 beta guides + FAQ so this is not tribal knowledge.

2025-05-10 (Liam O'Rourke, Support): Sent customer response using Colin’s draft + added disclaimer: “category list is authoritative for beta but may expand; no renames planned.” Customer asked one follow-up: can they export ONLY “audit_export.*” events to monitor changes to export config itself. I told them yes via action allowlist (exact match), pending confirmation from Eng on action strings.

2025-05-10 (Jordan Lee, Policy Eng): Confirmed: action filtering is exact match on action string. For export config audit events, action names are:
- audit_export.create
- audit_export.update
- audit_export.delete
- audit_export.rotate_credentials
- audit_export.test_connection
(Names are in schema v2; ensure customer understands rotate_credentials may be admin-only).

2025-05-13 (Colin O'Donnell, Solutions Engineer): Quantiva confirmed this meets their needs. They will start with allowlist of [audit_export.* actions + workspace role changes]. Reminder: they still want to minimize PII. We reiterated we can’t redact per-destination fields via filtering; redaction is applied at event emission per policy. If they need stricter controls, we should discuss category/action selection and confirm which events include IP/UA.

2025-05-14 (Liam O'Rourke, Support): Closing as Resolved. Outcome: provided taxonomy + examples; PM will incorporate into docs/FAQ. Next step is INT enablement ticket once they finalize destination settings.
resolution:
Provided customer-shareable category taxonomy overview, documented supported filtering predicates/limitations, and delivered concrete allowlist/denylist examples (admin-only, narrow action allowlist, auth exclusion). Clarified PII handling: cannot filter by field presence; redaction/minimization occurs at event type definition per policy. Identified exact action strings for audit_export.* to support a high-signal allowlist.

Docs follow-up: PM/Security to update beta FAQ + integration guides with category list + examples (tracked outside this ticket).
customer_facing_message: Thanks for the detailed questions. For the SIEM audit export beta, audit events include a stable category field (additive changes only during beta) and you can build filters using category allowlist/denylist and exact-match action allowlist/denylist, plus exact-match actor/resource identifiers. We’ll share recommended “starter filters” (e.g., admin/security-only, or a narrow allowlist of high-signal actions like workspace role changes and audit_export.*). Note: filtering does not support regex/prefix matching or filtering based on presence of optional fields like source_ip/user_agent; minimization/redaction is enforced at event emission per our audit logging policy.
internal_notes: If customer continues to push on “exclude any event with IP/UA,” we should route to Security (Marcus/Kevin) for an explicit statement of which event types include those fields and whether a config-level redaction option is on roadmap. Avoid promising per-destination field-level redaction during beta.
next_steps:
1) Docs: add category taxonomy + example filters to beta FAQ and Splunk/S3 guides (owner: Naomi + Docs + Security).
2) Once customer confirms final filters + destination, file internal enablement request (INT) to allowlist tenant and validate RBAC permissions.
3) Consider adding a short “high-signal action allowlist” snippet to Console UI helper text to reduce repeat tickets.
